facts.fact: The medina flourished under the Almohads and Hafsids from the twelfth to sixteenth centuries; UNESCO describes roughly 700 historic monuments of different types.
facts.excerpt: Under the Almohads and the Hafsids, from the 12th to the 16th century, Tunis was considered one of the greatest and wealthiest cities in the Islamic world. Some 700 monuments, including palaces, mosques, mausoleums, madrasas and fountains, testify to this remarkable past.
facts.location: Public page main heritage description; manually read November 1, 2026

facts.fact: The property includes a central medina and northern and southern suburbs; Bab Bhar and the Zitouna Mosque are named among its monuments.
facts.excerpt: It is composed of the central medina (8th century) and suburbs to the North and South (13th century).

facts.fact: UNESCO values the coherent urban fabric as well as individual buildings.
facts.excerpt: The attributes that express the Outstanding Universal Value include not only the buildings but also the coherent urban fabric of the town.
